title: Review Rust raw ownership reconstruction
why: Reconstructing an owner from a raw pointer requires matching provenance, allocator, layout, and exactly-once ownership.
suggestion: Keep the transfer local and document the originating into_raw contract, allocator, layout, and unique ownership.
limitations: The rule cannot prove pointer provenance, allocator compatibility, uniqueness, or lifetime correctness in general.

Direct matching Box, Rc, or Arc into_raw/from_raw transfers are excluded with no pointer conversion or a direct compiler-checked cast to a dyn trait-object pointer. Other pointer casts require an attached transparent-wrapper layout rationale. The original pointer must feed the same owner immediately and exactly once; pointer arithmetic, intermediate storage, owner-family changes, Vec raw-parts reconstruction, and arbitrary SAFETY comments do not establish this proof.
Borrowed slice and custom-qualified from_raw APIs are not ownership evidence. Locally shadowed standard type names, aliases, generic-qualified constructors, and wrapper functions are not resolved.
